transcript.text: Thanks everyone for joining. Let's get started on the Tuesday webhook incident postmortem. As we all know, duplicate webhook events were delivered to some customers for 26 minutes, triggered by a queue-worker deployment. No permanent payload loss has been confirmed. Before I can sign off on the remediation register, I need final status from each of the four owners — backend, SRE, security, and support. Let's go through what we have so far.

transcript.text: During a separate code review while tracing the worker deployment, I found an undocumented retry shortcut that bypasses the webhook idempotency key on the second attempt. I confirmed this behavior only shortly before this review and haven't filed the remediation ticket yet. This is likely the root cause behind the duplicate deliveries we saw on Tuesday.

transcript.text: I need to flag something on the SRE side. While checking an unrelated alert migration, I discovered that the duplicate-delivery alert has been disabled for ten days. The correct alert threshold for this service is 15 minutes — which means if the alert had been active, we should have caught this at 15 minutes instead of letting it run for 26 minutes. I haven't updated the monitoring ticket yet, but this clearly needs to be tracked as part of the remediation.
